svg.title: Multi-user governance
svg.desc: Messages from participants of a shared space pass the access gate, the pause check, reserved commands, a per-sender rate limit, the queue strategy and the model default for group sessions before an agent turn can create tasks. governance.admin_senders decides who may run reserved commands, review tasks and resolve run approvals, and is exempt from the limits.

g.text: Hover a box for its limit, exemption or audit rule; its connections light up. Click it to open its section.
Inside a rendered document this image is static. Click it to open the interactive SVG.

svg.text: Limits sit between a shared space and the task system, in this order; admin_senders decides who may command and review.

g.text: admitted by allowlists: Chat spaces, Slack channels, WhatsApp and Signal groups
Participants · senders admitted by an allowlist: Google Chat spaces, Slack channels, WhatsApp and Signal groups
Each sender is identified by the adapter (senderJid, senderDisplayName), so pause replay and task origin can attribute messages.
ChannelInboundGate · dm_access, group_access and require_mention decide; a refused message is dropped and logged
The gate is pure, so each adapter keeps its own logging and pairing effect. See the inbound pipeline figure.
PauseController · held messages replay on /resume as one collapsed message per conversation
In-memory, so a restart resets it. Capacity 200 plus max_pause_queued per sender (admins exempt); the bridge is skipped on replay.
ReservedCommandHandler · matches the exact command only and bypasses both pause queueing and rate limiting
A non-admin refusal sends the reply and writes one AuditEntry (guard ReservedCommand, hook channel_command); admin commands write none.
per_sender.messages per window; 0 disables; admins exempt
SlidingWindowRateLimiter · governance.rate_limits.per_sender.messages per window minutes, evaluated in the bridge
It runs before bound-thread routing, so a bound thread is no bypass; a refused sender gets a reply naming the limit.
fifo or fair; max_queued per sender, admins exempt
MessageQueue · governance.queue_strategy: fifo, or fair to rotate across senders so one user cannot monopolize a shared session
A full session queue or per-sender limit answers busy or queue full in the originating thread; the per-session cap is channels.max_queue_depth.
resolveChannelTurnOverrides · model and effort resolve per turn: row, sessions.channels, sessions.*, governance.crowd_coding
crowd_coding applies to group sessions only; the top-level crowd_coding key is ignored with a warning.
who may run reserved commands, review tasks
and resolve run approvals; empty list: everyone
governance.admin_senders · an empty list makes every sender an admin, which in a group lets every member approve or reject runs
An unidentified channel sender is an admin only where every sender is. The web caller is authenticated separately.
task_review · run approvals · task_review: accept, reject, push_back; a chat caller must be an admin and a delegated turn is refused
Run control audits every call (guard RunApprovalGate); Google Chat cards go through adminGatedReviewHandler (guard TaskReviewGate).
TaskOrigin · task_origin.dart: channelType, sessionKey, recipientId and optional contact and sender fields, under configJson origin
Lets notification subscribers post where the task came from and later turns carry the requester identity.
posts status changes to the origin
TaskNotificationSubscriber · posts on queued to running, running to review, review to accepted or rejected, and running to failed
A channel with ThreadedNotifications renders natively, one without gets plain sendMessage; a delivery never throws into its caller.
a bound thread routes to the task session
bound at first post, /bind or task_bind
thread binding · a bound thread routes its messages to the task session, after the rate limit
The binding is removed when the task reaches a terminal state or sits idle past idle_timeout_minutes (default 60).
